key_insight: A linearized convolution operator trained on LES mean profiles can learn interpretable, data-driven turbulent flux closures that outperform a standard K-profile approach across ABL stability regimes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more accurate and transparent flux parameterization for coarse atmospheric and climate models, improving prediction of momentum and heat exchange in unstable and stable boundary layers.
method: Train first-order closures on high-resolution LES of idealized flow over homogeneous surfaces.
Use nondimensional mean temperature and velocity profiles as inputs to predict nondimensional heat and momentum fluxes.
Select the best variant by minimizing mean squared error on training and unseen test cases; evaluate a posteriori in single-column simulations.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated across multiple stability regimes using LES training and test cases, and it remained stable in posteriori single-column simulations while closely matching LES profiles.
watch_item: Because the closure is learned from idealized homogeneous-surface LES, transfer to complex terrain, heterogeneous surfaces, or real atmospheric observations may require additional validation.
paper_title: Data-Driven Flux Parameterization for the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
